parts.title: My grandmother's bakery
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
My grandmother has a small bakery in the old part of town. It opened in 1985, and it has hardly changed since. The same wooden counter is there, and so are the same blue tiles on the wall. People come from all over the city for her chocolate cake.

When I was ten, I started to help her on Saturday mornings. At first I only washed trays, but she soon let me mix the eggs and the sugar. She never uses a machine. "Your hands know how long to mix," she says. I did not believe her until I made my first perfect cake.

The secret of the cake, she says, is the chocolate. She buys the best in the shop, even if it is expensive. She also puts a spoonful of coffee in the mixture. "You cannot taste it," she says, "but it makes the chocolate stronger."

Next year, I will leave for university, and I am afraid that I will miss the bakery. My grandmother just smiles and says that she will keep a piece of cake for me whenever I come home.

options: It is the biggest in the city
questions.explanation: It opened in 1985 and has hardly changed.

questions.explanation: At first he only washed trays.

questions.explanation: She never uses a machine; your hands know how long to mix.

questions.prompt: What is the secret of the cake?
options: A lot of sugar and butter

questions.explanation: She buys the best chocolate and adds a spoonful of coffee.

questions.prompt: How does the writer feel about next year?
options: Sure of a job in the shop
Afraid he will miss the bakery
questions.explanation: He is afraid that he will miss the bakery.

parts.title: The story of chocolate
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Chocolate comes from the seeds of the cacao tree. [1] Today, we think of it as a sweet food, but it was not always so.

The first people to use cacao were the Maya, in Central America, more than two thousand years ago. [2] They mixed the seeds with water and chilli to make a bitter, spicy drink.

When Spanish explorers arrived in the sixteenth century, they took cacao home to Europe. [3] They added sugar, which made the drink much sweeter, and soon it became fashionable among the rich.

The first solid chocolate bar appeared in England in 1847. [4] Before that, people could only drink it, and it was too expensive for most families.

Today, chocolate is made all over the world. [5] Experts say that each person in some countries eats about eight kilos of it a year.
sentences: It was one of the most important events in the history of food.
The tree grows only in warm, wet places near the equator.
It was so valuable that they used the seeds as money.
At first, Europeans did not like the taste.
People never seem to get tired of this sweet food.
Some people cannot eat it because of an allergy.

gaps.explanation: The tree grows only in warm places, which leads on to how we think of chocolate today.
The seeds were so valuable that they were used as money, and the next sentence says what the Maya did with them.
At first Europeans did not like the taste, so they added sugar.
The first chocolate bar was one of the most important events, and the next sentence says before that people could only drink it.
People never get tired of this sweet food, and the next sentence gives how much people eat.

parts.title: A message about a recipe
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Hi Tom, Thank you for the cake recipe. I made it on Sunday, and my family loved it! I followed the instructions [1] carefully, but the middle was still a bit soft. Perhaps my oven is not [2] hot as yours. Next time, I will cook it for ten minutes longer. My little sister wanted to help, so I [3] her break the eggs. She made a bit of a mess, [4] she was very proud of herself. Could you send me the recipe for the chocolate sauce too? I think it would taste lovely [5] the cake. I will bring you a piece [6] I see you at school on Monday. Best wishes, Clara

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: Very carefully is an adverb phrase.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: Not as hot as yours: a comparison.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: Let her break the eggs: permission.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: A mess, but she was proud: contrast.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: On the cake means placed on top of it.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: When I see you at school on Monday: a time.

parts.title: Too many sweets?
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Many children love sweets, but eating too many is bad for your teeth. Dentists say that it is not only the sugar, but also how often we eat sweet things, [1] matters. If you eat sweets all day, your teeth have no time to recover. It is better to eat them after a meal, [2] you have more saliva in your mouth. Drinking water also helps to wash away the sugar. You should brush your teeth [3] least twice a day, in the morning and before bed. Some sweets are better than others. Dark chocolate, [4] example, has less sugar than milk chocolate. The worst sweets are the sticky ones, [5] they stay on the teeth for a long time. Remember, you do not have to stop eating them completely. You just need to [6] careful.

gaps.explanation: It is how often we eat sweet things that matters: a cleft sentence.
After a meal because you have more saliva: a reason.
At least twice a day: a fixed phrase.
Because they stay on the teeth: a reason.
Need to be careful: the infinitive of be.

parts.title: A talk at a chocolate factory
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: nathalie
turns.text: Welcome to our chocolate factory. My name is Carys, and I will be your guide today. We make about twenty thousand bars every day, and we send them to forty countries. The factory was started by a family of bakers in 1920. Today, it is still owned by the same family. First, we will see how the cacao beans arrive from Ghana. They are cleaned, then roasted in big ovens for about an hour. After that, they are crushed into a thick paste. The paste is mixed with sugar and milk, and then it is stirred for three days to make it smooth. Finally, the chocolate is poured into shapes and cooled. At the end of the tour, you can try three different kinds. Please do not touch the machines, and remember that photographs are only allowed in the shop. Shall we begin?

gaps.prompt: The factory makes about ___ bars every day
gaps.explanation: We make about twenty thousand bars every day.

gaps.prompt: The chocolate is sent to ___ countries
gaps.explanation: We send them to forty countries.
The factory was started by a family of bakers in 1920.
The cacao beans arrive from Ghana.

gaps.prompt: The mixture is stirred for ___ days
gaps.explanation: It is stirred for three days to make it smooth.

gaps.prompt: Visitors can try ___ kinds of chocolate
gaps.explanation: At the end of the tour, you can try three different kinds.

parts.title: An interview with a pastry chef
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Colm, you make desserts for a famous hotel. How did you get the job?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I started as a kitchen helper when I was seventeen. I watched the chefs and asked a lot of questions. Four years later they gave me my own place.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the most popular dessert in the hotel?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Definitely the chocolate fondant. It is warm in the middle, and people always ask for the recipe. I never give it!

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the hardest part of your work?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Timing. A dessert must be ready exactly when the main course finishes, so the whole kitchen has to work together.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you eat a lot of sweet food yourself?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Surprisingly, no. I taste everything I make, but just a little. At home, I prefer cheese and fruit.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you do on your days off?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I go hiking in the hills. After a week in a hot kitchen, I need fresh air and some quiet.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you have a message for young people who want to be chefs?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Be patient and be curious. Everyone makes mistakes. The ones who learn from them become the best.
